Proof of (3). Observe that <MATH_0001> has a covering by the affine
opens <MATH_0002> for <MATH_0003>. The rings <MATH_0004> are Jacobson by
More on Algebra, Lemma
<REF_0001>.
Hence <MATH_0005> is Jacobson by
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Parts (1) and (2) are special cases of (3).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Direct proof of case (1).
Since <MATH_0006> is a Noetherian scheme,
<MATH_0007> is a Noetherian scheme (Lemma <REF_0003>).
Hence <MATH_0008> is a sober, Noetherian topological space (use
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0004>).
Assume <MATH_0009> is not Jacobson to
get a contradiction. By
Topology, Lemma <REF_0005>
there exists some non-closed point <MATH_0010>
such that <MATH_0011> is locally closed. This corresponds
to a prime <MATH_0012> such that (1) there exists
a prime <MATH_0013>, <MATH_0014>
with both inclusions strict, and (2) <MATH_0015> is open in
<MATH_0016>. This is impossible by Algebra,
Lemma <REF_0006>.
